title: When stability becomes a liability: the negative effects of supplier network stability on green innovation diversity and quality
summary: Purpose Drawing on the network embeddedness perspective, this study aims to investigate how supplier network stability affects two distinct facets of green innovation – diversity and quality – and how these relationships are moderated by absorptive capacity. Design/methodology/approach The proposed relationships are tested using ordinary least squares regression based on a sample of 1,655 firm-year observations from 577 Chinese publicly listed firms over the period 2009–2023. To address potential endogeneity and selection bias, we conduct a series of analyses. Findings We find that supplier network stability is detrimental to both green innovation diversity and green innovation quality. Furthermore, absorptive capacity plays a differential moderating role, alleviating the detrimental influence of supplier network stability on green innovation quality while having no significant moderating effect on green innovation diversity. Originality/value By integrating the network embeddedness perspective with the green innovation literature, this study uncovers the unintended consequences of supplier network stability for green innovation diversity and quality and underscores the important role of absorptive capacity in mitigating these adverse effects.

title: Risk Exposure and Institutional Pressure: Drivers of Environmental Disclosure in Sub‐Saharan Africa
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates how objective environmental and institutional pressures drive corporate environmental disclosure in sub‐Saharan Africa, independent of firms' self‐reported claims. Using 2390 firm‐year observations (2012–2021) from six countries, we proxy for carbon intensity and occupational safety risk using sector‐level benchmarks from the International Energy Agency, the International Labour Organisation and for regulatory stringency using the World Bank's policy index. Findings indicate that firms in high‐risk sectors disclose significantly more, and stronger national regulations further increase transparency, even under weak enforcement. These results refine legitimacy and institutional theories by demonstrating that disclosure responds to measurable risk exposure rather than merely symbolic reporting. We find that grounding analysis in observable risk exposures strengthens environmental accountability in emerging markets. The findings support risk‐proportionate disclosure mandates: stringent, verified reporting for high‐impact sectors and streamlined requirements for low‐risk firms, enhancing relevance without overburdening institutions.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Resilience on Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
summary: Against a backdrop of frequent external shocks and an accelerating green transition, this study examines whether supply chain resilience improves firms' current green innovation. Using 2004-2024 panel data for Chinese A-share listed firms, we construct supply chain resilience as the sum of entropy-weighted resistance and recovery indices. Two-way fixed-effects estimates show that all three measures significantly increase green patent applications. The findings remain robust to leave-one-out industry-year instrumental-variable estimation, alternative samples, expanded controls, and an alternative resilience measure. Mechanism tests indicate that resilience supports green R&D by easing financing constraints and reducing agency costs, while corporate reputation and ownership concentration improve the conversion of resilience resources into innovation. The effect differs across listing boards, ownership types, and factor intensities: it is stronger for non-GEM, state-owned, and labor-intensive firms, but becomes negative for GEM firms. Supply chain resilience is therefore not merely an operational safeguard; it is also an organizational capability that sustains green innovation. The evidence provides a firm-level basis for jointly advancing supply chain security and green transformation.

title: Corporate disclosures of carbon-reduction actions and firm value: the moderating role of digital transformation
summary: Purpose This study examines whether corporate disclosures of carbon-reduction actions are associated with firm value under China's “dual-carbon” strategy. It further compares the valuation relevance of internally oriented operational disclosures and value-chain-oriented disclosures and investigates the moderating role of digital transformation. Design/methodology/approach Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2023, this study develops a machine-learning-assisted textual measurement approach to identify disclosures of carbon-reduction actions from annual reports, environmental, social and governance (ESG) reports and sustainability reports. Fixed-effects regressions are employed to test valuation effects, with additional analyses on moderating effects, mediating mechanisms and firm heterogeneity. Findings Corporate disclosures of carbon-reduction actions are positively associated with firm value. This association is stronger for internally oriented operational disclosures than for value-chain-oriented disclosures. Digital transformation negatively moderates both associations. Channel tests provide evidence consistent with three mechanisms: improved trade credit, stronger media reputation and enhanced green innovation. Practical implications Firms should improve differentiated carbon disclosure across emission scopes and coordinate resource allocation across digital and green initiatives. Policymakers should strengthen disclosure standards and provide targeted support for small and medium-sized firms to enhance collaborative carbon reduction and green innovation. Originality/value This study introduces an emission-scope-informed perspective into research on the market valuation of carbon-reduction disclosures and develops a machine-learning-assisted approach for identifying firm-level disclosures of carbon-reduction actions.

title: Seeing Is More than Believing: ESG Performance Aspiration Gap and Institutional Investors’ Site Visits
summary: ESG has profoundly influenced asset pricing and resource allocation in capital markets. However, existing research largely focuses on the economic consequences of absolute ESG levels, with limited attention paid to how the gap between corporate ESG performance and aspiration levels—the ESG performance aspiration gap—is related to the behavior of information intermediaries in the capital market. Using a sample of A-share non-financial listed companies on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange from 2013 to 2024, this paper empirically examines the relation between the ESG performance aspiration gap and institutional investors’ site visits and its potential underlying channel. The findings are as follows. First, the ESG performance aspiration gap is positively correlated with institutional investors’ site visits. This conclusion remains robust after a series of robustness tests. Second, the mechanism analysis is consistent with information asymmetry serving as a potential channel linking the ESG performance aspiration gap and institutional investors’ site visits. Third, the moderating effect analysis shows that both marketization level and analyst coverage negatively moderate the positive relation between the ESG performance aspiration gap and institutional investors’ site visits. This paper extends the research boundaries of the economic consequences of ESG and institutional investors’ information search behavior, providing a new theoretical explanation for how the capital market responds to the dynamic changes in corporate ESG performance. It also offers policy implications for improving the ESG information disclosure system and enhancing the information efficiency of the capital market.

title: Corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, political connections, and tax avoidance in a developing country: A systematic literature review of Indonesian evidence
summary: Tax avoidance is a central corporate-governance and fiscal issue in developing countries, where tax revenues are important but enforcement and governance quality remain heterogeneous. This systematic literature review synthesizes Indonesian corporate evidence on Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), political connections, and tax avoidance. Following the PRISMA 2020 logic, the review documented 14 records identified through Google Scholar and SINTA searches conducted with Publish or Perish, supplemented by Scopus and Web of Science verification. After screening and eligibility assessment, 11 primary empirical studies were retained and three records were excluded as out-of-scope or secondary/contextual literature. The synthesis indicates that political connections are the most consistently reported positive correlate of tax avoidance, although the relationship is not universal. Conventional GCG proxies do not consistently reduce tax avoidance in isolation, while CSR produces ambivalent results that are consistent with both an ethical-constraint mechanism and a legitimacy-shield mechanism. Firmansyah et al. (2022) provides particularly strong evidence: political connections and investment opportunity sets increase tax avoidance, whereas CSR disclosure weakens those positive effects. Measurement heterogeneity, especially differences among ETR, CETR, BTD, and related proxies, contributes to divergent findings. The review concludes with implications for tax-risk profiling, governance evaluation, and future causal research.

title: Unleashing Green Vitality: The Impact of the Digital Economy on Green Innovation in Resource-Based Cities
summary: Resource-based cities are often characterized by concentrated industrial structures, energy-intensive production, and substantial pressure for technological transformation. Whether digitalization can strengthen green technological innovation in these cities remains an important empirical question. Using a balanced panel of 114 Chinese resource-based cities over the period 2011–2019, this study evaluates the implications of digital economy development for green technological innovation. The empirical strategy combines two-way fixed-effects estimation with alternative measurements, dynamic panel estimation, instrumental-variable identification, and a quasi-natural experiment based on the “Broadband China” policy. The estimates consistently indicate that digital development increases green patenting in resource-based cities. Further evidence is consistent with a potential financial-development channel whereby digitalization may relax financing constraints and improve the allocation of financial resources toward innovation-oriented activities. The estimated impact is also amplified when environmental issues receive greater attention from local governments and the public. Nonlinear estimation identifies two critical values for both digital development and marketization, with the marginal innovation return to digitalization rising after each threshold is crossed. Taken together, the results show that digitalization can facilitate the technological transformation of resource-dependent economies, but its effectiveness is contingent on complementary financial capacity, environmental governance, and market institutions.

title: ESG Disclosure and Real Earnings Management in High-Polluting Industries: The Moderating Role of Audit Quality
summary: The current research looks at how Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) disclosure affects real earnings management (REM) and how audit quality (AQ) moderates this relationship. The study sample consists of 292 firm-year observations for the period 2022–2025 from 73 non-financial firms in highly polluting industries listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul). Panel regression analyses and an alternative estimator (pooled OLS with robust standard errors) are used to assess the robustness of the results. The findings show that REM is negatively associated with ESG disclosure, suggesting that firms with higher ESG disclosure have lower REM. However, the moderating hypothesis (H2) is not supported by the present evidence since the interaction between ESG disclosure and AQ is not statistically significant in any of the specifications estimated. The absence of a significant interaction is viewed as a lack of statistically measurable moderation as specified here. Based on an integrated Agency and Stakeholder Theory framework, the study considers ESG disclosure and AQ as mechanisms that increase the expected penalty for managerial opportunism and the expected probability of detection, respectively, and therefore suggests a positive relationship between the two; hence, the two mechanisms were expected to act as complements, not substitutes. The evidence confirms the first mechanism, but there is no evidence for the conjunction, indicating that the complementarity is conditional and is not yet available in the Saudi environment because of the lack of an assurance mandate for non-financial information. The study provides new insights from an emerging market and establishes the limitations of ESG disclosure and audit quality in limiting REM together.

summary: This thesis analyzes the role of institutional investors (non-state pension funds, insurance companies, and investment funds) in the capital market of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the challenges associated with attracting them. title: Exploring the Potential of Green Finance: a Narrative Literature Review
summary: Objective: Investigate the potential of green finance in order to explore its impact on environmental sustainability and the financial performance of companies. Theoretical Framework: The fundamental concepts underpinning the research are presented, with a focus on green finance, sustainable investments, green bonds, and ESG criteria. This provides a solid basis for understanding the research context. Method: The research was conducted through a narrative review of the literature with a bibliographic and qualitative nature, involving scientific references in the Google Scholar and CAPES periodical databases. A total of 45 relevant publications were selected from the database using a combination of keywords to present the results of this study. Results and Discussion: The findings indicate that green finance implementations exert a favorable influence on environmental sustainability, underscoring the efficacy of green financial instruments in promoting sustainable projects and, consequently, fostering renewable energy production and enhancing energy efficiency. The analysis further indicates a growing body of literature on green finance, underscoring the importance of sustainable finance in the current global context. Research Implications: The practical and theoretical implications of this research reflect on how green finance can be integrated into business strategies and influence practices in the field of financial management, contributing to sustainability. Originality/Value: It contributes to the literature by offering a comprehensive review of green finance, highlighting its relevance in a growing context of environmental concern and the need for responsible financial practices.

title: Audit committee characteristics, corporate environmental sustainability and earnings management strategy: An empirical study of Saudi Arabia-listed companies
summary: This study aimed to explore the link between audit committee (AC) characteristics and earnings management (EM) in Saudi listed companies and assess the effect of corporate environmental sustainability (assessed using corporate social responsibility (CSR)-related measures) on the relationship between the two. The study draws data from a panel of 131 firms listed on the Saudi Exchange from 2015 to 2021, comprising 917 firm-year observations. In the baseline model, the results show that meetings between the AC and the board are negatively related to EM. In the baseline analysis, however, there were no significant effects on the size and independence of the AC. Furthermore, the moderating analysis shows that the interaction between CSR and AC size is positive and statistically significant, while the interaction between CSR and AC independence is positive and marginally significant. However, the relationship between CSR and AC meetings is not statistically significant. The results indicate that the effect of AC characteristics on EM is dependent on firms’ CSR involvement. The results from the robustness tests conducted using feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimations also give results similar to those of the baseline model, which ensures the reliability and stability of the main findings.

title: Developing environmental performance in the Bangladesh banking sector: role of fintech, climate finance and environmental awareness
summary: This study aims to investigate the relationship between climate banking and the environmental performance of banks in Bangladesh, focusing on climate finance, environmental awareness, and the role of FinTech. The study used the partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) technique to analyse data from 312 bank practitioners. The results revealed that climate banking practices (CBP) are positively associated with climate finance (CF), environmental awareness (EA), and FinTech adoption (FA). CF and FA are positively related to the bank’s environmental performance (BEP), while EA determines both direct and indirect associations with BEP. FA and CF play a mediating role in the relationship between CBP and BEP. This research contributes to the first empirical understanding of how digital transformation and climate-aligned financing mechanisms can promptly promote sustainability in the Global South banking sector context. This builds the groundwork for understanding how increased climate change resilience can contribute to the sustainability and global competitiveness of banks in emerging economies. This also aids policymakers and banks in developing convergence strategies with global frameworks for sustainable development.

title: Financial and institutional pathways through which green finance and sustainable investment support the transition toward low-carbon economies
summary: This paper examines the relationship between green finance, sustainable investment and the transition toward low-carbon economies by reviewing the main theoretical and empirical contributions developed in recent literature. The analysis focuses on three complementary dimensions: the institutional and financial foundations of green finance, the integration of sustainability and climate risk into investment and asset-pricing decisions, and the capacity of sustainable finance to generate measurable changes in production, technological adoption and economic decarbonization. The reviewed studies show that green bonds, green loans, ESG-oriented investment and climate-related financial policies can influence capital allocation, but their effectiveness depends strongly on credible certification, transparent information, appropriate risk-sharing mechanisms and supportive institutional frameworks. The literature also indicates that carbon exposure and climate risk are progressively incorporated into asset prices and portfolio decisions, while investor preferences increasingly affect demand for environmentally responsible securities. Beyond financial markets, the evidence suggests that green finance can support renewable-energy deployment, green technological investment, sustainable supply-chain practices and improvements in green total factor productivity. The overall conclusion is that sustainable finance contributes most effectively to low-carbon transition when financial development is translated into concrete technological, organizational and productive changes capable of reducing the environmental intensity of economic activity.

title: Smart supply chains: industry 4.0 and resilience in the UAE food and beverage sector
summary: Introduction The United Arab Emirates (UAE) food and beverage (F&B) sector is structurally import-dependent and critical to national industrial diversification, food security, and circular economy goals, making supply chain resilience a strategic priority. This study investigates how the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies (Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, cyber-physical systems, and cloud computing) enhances supply chain resilience. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Dynamic Resource-Based View, and Supply Chain Resilience Theory, the research posits that Industry 4.0 adoption impacts resilience directly and indirectly via supply chain and dynamic capabilities as mediators, with digital organizational culture acting as a moderator. Methods A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was utilized, gathering data via a structured survey administered to 395 senior supply chain and operations managers within UAE F&B manufacturing companies. The collected dataset was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS with 5,000 resamples to evaluate measurement validity, structural paths, and moderation effects. Results The structural equation modeling results support all six hypothesized paths. Industry 4.0 technology adoption exerts a significant positive effect on supply chain capabilities ( β = 0.849, P < 0.01$) and dynamic capabilities ( β = 0.869, P < 0.01$). Both supply chain capabilities ( β = 0.735, P < 0.01$) and dynamic capabilities ( β = 0.769, P < 0.01$) positively influence supply chain resilience. Furthermore, Industry 4.0 adoption has a direct positive impact on resilience ( β = 0.856, P < 0.01$), and digital organizational culture positively moderates the technology-resilience relationship ( β = 0.729, P < 0.01$). Discussion The findings demonstrate that modernizing F&B supply chains requires more than standalone technological investments; digital tools must be combined with internal capability building and a supportive digital organizational culture. For UAE producers, leveraging solutions like IoT traceability and AI forecasting—underpinned by a data-driven culture—strengthens overall network adaptability and recovery. These insights align with national strategic frameworks such as the UAE Circular Economy Policy 2021–2031 and Operation 300bn.

title: The ESG−audit nexus: unpacking the mediating role of CSR strategy and contextual moderators
summary: Purpose This research aims to investigate the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) scores on the likelihood of conducting sustainability audits. In this context, the mediating role of corporate social responsibility (CSR) strategy and the moderating roles of company size and systematic risk are considered. Design/methodology/approach This study used panel data from 168,198 firm-year observations. Findings A positive and significant relationship was found between the overall ESG score and the likelihood of conducting sustainability audits. Additionally, the mediating role of the CSR strategy was confirmed, indicating that formalized CSR commitments facilitate the translation of ESG performance into sustainability audits. Moreover, company size and systematic risk, as moderating variables, strengthened the aforementioned relationship. Originality/value This study integrates and extends institutional theory (focusing on external pressures for ESG) and strategic choice perspective (focusing on internal CSR strategy) to explain corporate behavior. title: PRIORITY DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE CORPORATE GOVERNANCE MECHANISMS OF CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRY ENTERPRISES UNDER DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: The article examines the improvement of the corporate governance mechanisms of construction industry enterprises under the conditions of digital transformation. The relevance of the research lies in the fact that the introduction of digital tools does not in itself raise the quality of governance: an effect arises only when these tools are connected to the procedures for taking decisions. The author proposes a model of the impact of digital transformation on governance mechanisms through three channels — the information, control and decision channels — together with a matrix for selecting priority directions according to the expected effect and the complexity of implementation.
